repo_notes.content: eventflow-payment-service is System 2 of the EventFlow demo and a consumer of the shared demo-ledger-service library (same GitHub organisation), pinned to a Git tag in pyproject.toml. It uses ledger.fees.management_fee to attach a processing-fee line to every completed payment. The sibling eventflow-order-service consumes the same library for settlement dates. The zero-decimal currency (JPY/KRW) conversion bug in app/processor.py is an intentional demo narrative; do not describe it as fixed unless the code changes.

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: What the Payment Service does: consumes OrderCreated events from Azure Service Bus, converts minor-unit amounts to display amounts, validates them against per-currency minimum thresholds, simulates a gateway call, records a PaymentRecord (with processing fee) and calls back to the Order Service to update order status. Include the architecture diagram from the README.

pages.title: Payment Processing Pipeline
pages.purpose: app/processor.py end to end: convert_to_display_amount, validate_payment_amount, process_payment_through_gateway, process_order_payment; the PaymentRecord model; and the documented zero-decimal currency bug used in the demo narrative.

pages.title: Processing Fee via demo-ledger-service
pages.purpose: How app/fees.py wraps ledger.fees.management_fee (25 bps, Decimal, rounded to the cent), where the fee appears on PaymentRecord, how the dependency is pinned (git + tag in pyproject.toml), how to upgrade the pin, why Dockerfile installs git, and where the library's accounting conventions are documented.

pages.title: Service Bus Consumer and Configuration
pages.purpose: app/consumer.py background thread, message handling and error paths, the order-status callback, app/config.py settings and environment variables.

pages.title: Development, Testing and CI/CD
pages.purpose: Poetry setup, running locally, pytest and ruff, the GitHub Actions ci.yml (test + docker build) and cd.yml (Azure Container Apps deploy).
